In France, the social security system ensures that prenatal and postnatal medical care in public hospitals comes at no cost. Working mothers receive 16 weeks of maternity leave with daily payments between €9.29 and €84.90, depending on their previous income levels. During pregnancy and childbirth periods, financial concerns remain consistent with normal times - struggling families continue to face difficulties while prosperous families maintain their comfortable status.

However, support for new mothers falls short of expectations. Fathers only receive 11 days of leave, which doesn't provide adequate time for mothers to heal from delivery. Consequently, new mothers face the challenge of managing constant newborn care while recovering physically. They also encounter difficulties finding suitable childcare, as government programs prove inadequate, particularly around Paris.

Childcare expenses vary significantly across options. Public daycare centers charge low-income families approximately €1,000 annually, yet they accommodate only one child for every eight applicants. This shortage forces families to rely on private alternatives like nannies or in-home caregivers.
